proposer_argument.content:
POSITION
Claim A (Moctezuma II was the Aztec ruler when the Spanish arrived)

EVIDENCE REVIEW
Claim A: Moctezuma II was the Aztec ruler when the Spanish arrived in 1519 according to historical records.
Claim B: Andrés de Tapia Motelchiuh was the Aztec ruler appointed by the Spanish when they arrived in 1519.

REASONING
The core issue is determining who held the position of Aztec ruler at the time of Hernán Cortés' arrival in 1519. Historical consensus identifies Moctezuma II as the ninth tlatoani (ruler) of the Aztec Empire who was in power when the Spanish first arrived. In contrast, Andrés de Tapia was a Spanish conquistador and chronicler, not an Aztec ruler. There is no historical evidence that an Aztec ruler named Andrés de Tapia Motelchiuh existed or that he was appointed by the Spanish as their ruler over the Aztecs.

REASONING
The fundamental issue is identifying who held the position of Aztec ruler during the Spanish arrival. Historical evidence clearly shows Moctezuma II was the ninth tlatoani (ruler) of the Aztec Empire when Cortés arrived in 1519, while Andrés de Tapia was a Spanish conquistador and chronicler, not an Aztec ruler. The claim that Tapia was appointed as ruler by the Spanish lacks historical support and contradicts established facts about the Aztec leadership structure.

SOURCE BASIS
The evidence is based on established historical records documenting Moctezuma II's reign as Aztec ruler from approximately 1502-1520, and historical accounts that identify Andrés de Tapia solely as a Spanish conquistador who participated in the conquest but never held indigenous Aztec leadership positions.

CONCLUSION
Moctezuma II was the Aztec ruler when the Spanish arrived in 1519.

proposer_argument.content:
POSITION
Claim A (Moctezuma II was the Aztec ruler when the Spanish arrived)

EVIDENCE REVIEW
Claim A: Moctezuma II was the Aztec ruler when the Spanish arrived in 1519 according to historical records.
Claim B: Andrés de Tapia Motelchiuh was the Aztec ruler appointed by the Spanish when they arrived in 1519.

REASONING
The core issue is determining who held the position of Aztec ruler at the time of Hernán Cortés' arrival in 1519. Historical consensus identifies Moctezuma II as the ninth tlatoani (ruler) of the Aztec Empire who was in power when the Spanish first arrived. In contrast, Andrés de Tapia was a Spanish conquistador and chronicler, not an Aztec ruler. There is no historical evidence that an Aztec ruler named Andrés de Tapia Motelchiuh existed or that he was appointed by the Spanish as their ruler over the Aztecs.

REASONING
The fundamental issue is identifying who held the position of Aztec ruler during the Spanish arrival. Historical evidence clearly shows Moctezuma II was the ninth tlatoani (ruler) of the Aztec Empire when Cortés arrived in 1519, while Andrés de Tapia was a Spanish conquistador and chronicler, not an Aztec ruler. The claim that Tapia was appointed as ruler by the Spanish lacks historical support and contradicts established facts about the Aztec leadership structure.

SOURCE BASIS
The evidence is based on established historical records documenting Moctezuma II's reign as Aztec ruler from approximately 1502-1520, and historical accounts that identify Andrés de Tapia solely as a Spanish conquistador who participated in the conquest but never held indigenous Aztec leadership positions.

CONCLUSION
Moctezuma II was the Aztec ruler when the Spanish arrived in 1519.
